notes_for_us: This prompt is mostly timers - 30-second despawns, 1-2 minute respawns, a 5-minute OG cycle - and the triage rule sends all of it to mechanics, correctly. But the user also asked for a 3D countdown display showing that timer, which is geometry, and there is no option for a readout built into the world. The same request splits across two piles and only one of them has anywhere to go.

The no-2D-UI rule is the most load-bearing sentence in the prompt and it lands in constraints, where nothing downstream is obliged to honour it. It should probably force physical station options rather than sit as prose - as written, a build could satisfy every option in the handoff and still put the shop on screen.

spawner-npc was the only row for a machine that emits pets, and the universal-options note explicitly warns against using it for anything non-hostile. Following that warning would have left the central object of the game with no ID at all, so I used it against the note and said so.

winner-zone is inferred: the genre says the run ends somewhere and the prompt never says where, so the last stage terminates in a reward area rather than simply stopping.
Rainbow Fly lets players bypass stages by air, which means the course should read as clearable from above without breaking - worth knowing at generation time even though flight itself is mechanics.

notes_for_us: Two thirds of this prompt is scripting and monetisation, and the triage rule handled it without strain - mechanics took all of it and the map is not worse for it. This is the case the skill's tower-defense example describes, and it worked.

The one thing with no home is the shop, because the user was specific that it is a GUI on screen. Obby has social-hub for a start hub with a shop and using it would have built a building the prompt did not ask for, so the request is recorded and dropped. The enriched expansion built the kiosk anyway, which is the failure the destination field exists to catch.

Theme came out null and I could not read one from the prompt: lava and coils are obby furniture, not a setting. That is the rule working, but it means a prompt this detailed still cannot say what its map looks like.
